title: Protocol for isolation of microbiota-derived membrane vesicles from mouse blood and colon
protocol: Euthanize mice by cervical dislocation for blood collection.
Disinfect the front of the mouse from the neck to the belly region with a paper towel soaked in 70% ethanol.
Make an incision using sharp, sterile scissors at the end of the sternum and near the diaphragm to access the thoracic cavity.
Insert one blade of scissors into the opening at the position of the sternum.
To open the thoracic cavity, cut through the rib cage.
Bend the ribs to the side to expose the heart.
Attach a sterile filter tip to a micropipette and puncture the atrium of the heart.
Carefully draw blood from the heart while avoiding clogging the pipet tip.
Collect clots alongside with the blood if premature clotting occurs.
Transfer the collected blood into a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube at room temperature (20°C).
Mix the blood by inverting the tube 5 times.
Incubate the collected blood at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the blood at 1,500 ×g and 4°C for 10 minutes to separate serum from blood cells/clot.
Carefully transfer the upper phase (serum) to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube by avoiding touching the blood clot.
Centrifuge the serum again at 1,500 ×g and 4°C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the upper phase of the serum to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Store the serum on ice until further processing.
Euthanatize mice by cervical dislocation.
Disinfect the front of the mouse from the sternum to the anus with a paper towel soaked in 70% ethanol.
Make a ventral incision between the sternum and anus using sharp, sterile scissors.
Remove the skin pelt by tearing it in the transverse plane.
Open the peritoneal cavity carefully without cutting any inner organs.
Grasp the pyloric sphincter and set aside the stomach with the small intestine until reaching the cecum.
Cut below the cecum to separate the colon from other intestinal segments.
Grasp the proximal colon and cut the rectum to isolate it.
Place the isolated colon into a sterile Petri dish.
Apply gentle pressure on the colon to guide the luminal content out of its cavity.
Collect the luminal content with a sterile spatula into a 50 mL reaction tube containing ice-cold DPBS.
Store samples on ice until further processing.
Vortex the colon content for 30 seconds at approximately 1500 rpm (speed position 6; Test tube shakers Genie Vortex Mixer Model: Vortex-Genie 2).
Pellet colon luminal content at 4,000 ×g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 15 mL reaction tube.
Centrifuge supernatant at 4,000 ×g, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 15 mL reaction tube.
Repeat step c by spinning the supernatant at 4,000 ×g, 4°C for 10 minutes and transferring it to a new 15 mL reaction tube.
Spin the supernatant at 6,000 ×g, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 15 mL reaction tube.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.45 μm syringe filter into a new 15 mL reaction tube.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.2 μm syringe filter into a new 15 mL reaction tube.
Hold the colon content fluid on ice while equilibrating filter devices.
Seal the filter device with the filtrate collection tube.
Load the sample into the filter device.
Add the concentrate collection tube on top of the filter device and push down to seal.
Insert the sealed filter device into the centrifuge rotor until the rim of the concentrate collection tube is inside the centrifuge rotor well.
Remove the whole filter device from the rotor.
Disconnect the filter device from the filtrate collection tube.
Invert the filter device with sealed concentrate collection tube.
Insert the inverted filter device with sealed concentrate collection tube into the centrifuge rotor and spin.
Take the filter device with sealed concentrate collection tube out of the rotor.
Disconnect the concentrate collection tube containing the concentrated serum or colon fluid from the filter device.
Equilibrate each Amicon Ultra-2 centrifugal filter device with 500 μL ice-cold, sterile filtered DPBS.
Place the Amicon Ultra-2 filtrate devices into the filtrate collection tubes.
Confirm that the filtrate devices are properly sealed in the collection tubes.
Load each filtrate device with 500 μL ice-cold, sterile filtered DPBS.
Cover the filtrate devices with the concentrate collection tubes by pushing the collection tubes onto the filtrate devices.
Place the filter devices into the centrifuge with swinging buckets.
Ensure that the filter devices are in contact with the bottom of the rotor.
Make sure the rims of the concentrate collection tubes are inside the centrifuge rotor well.
Centrifuge at 4,000 ×g and 4°C for 60 minutes.
Remove the filter devices from the centrifuge.
Disconnect the filter devices from the filtrate collection tubes containing the flow-through.
Discard the flow-through in the collection devices.
Seal the filter devices again in the collection tubes.
Use DPBS-equilibrated Amicon Ultra-2 centrifugal filter devices to load the serum and colon fluid for subsequent concentration.
Remove the concentrate collection tube from the filter device.
Load each filtrate device with 1.5 mL ice-cold serum or 1.5 mL ice-cold colon fluid.
Cover the filtrate devices with the concentrate collection tubes by pushing the collection tubes onto the filtrate devices.
Place the filter devices into the centrifuge rotor as described above.
Centrifuge at 4,000 ×g and 4°C for 60 minutes.
Remove filter devices from the centrifuge.
Disconnect filter devices from filtrate collection tubes.
Invert filter devices tied to concentrate collection tubes and place them in the centrifuge rotor, counterbalancing as necessary.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g and 4°C for 2 minutes.
Remove concentrate collection tubes from the filter devices.
Transfer concentrated samples from each filter device into a 1.5 mL low protein binding collection tube.
Hold concentrated samples on ice.
Prepare qEVoriginal / 70 nm Gen 2 columns as directed for use.
Load 500 μL of pre-concentrated serum or colon fluid onto the column.
Collect eluted fractions in volumes of 0.5 mL each.
Consider fractions 1–6 as void volume fractions.
Collect MVs from fractions 7 to 9 where they are expected to elute.
Collect protein fractions primarily in fractions 10 to 12.
Let qEVoriginal / 70 nm Gen 2 columns and sterile filtered DPBS reach working temperature of 20°C.
Insert qEVoriginal / 70 nm Gen 2 columns into the column stand provided by IZON.
Equilibrate each column with at least 40 mL of sterile-filtered DPBS.
Open upper cap of a column and add 2 mL sterile-filtered DPBS to the filter on top of the column resin (top-filter).
Remove luer slip cap and collect flow-through in the 15 mL reaction tube below the column.
Continuously add DPBS to columns but not more than 2 mL at a time until each column is equilibrated with at least 40 mL DPBS.
Empty 15 mL reaction tube for collecting flow-through whenever required.
Add luer slip cap to close the column from bottom when equilibration is complete to avoid loss of buffer volume.
Open the upper cap of a qEVoriginal / 70 nm Gen 2 column.
Remove buffer above the top-filter while leaving the luer slip cap on the column.
Load 500 μL of concentrated serum or colon fluid onto the center of the filter.
Remove the luer slip cap and start collecting 0.5 mL fractions in low protein binding collection tubes.
Collect the first 6 fractions containing the void volume.
Save time by collecting the first 6 fractions in two 1.5 mL collection tubes.
Add DPBS on the top-filter to level the filter, avoiding unintentional dilution of the sample.
Do not let the filter run dry and do not add more than 2 mL DPBS on the top-filter.
Collect fractions 7 to 9 separately containing the highest amount of MVs.
Store collected fractions 7 to 9 at 4°C.
Collect further fractions up to 12 that are supposed to contain higher protein content and low membrane vesicles.
Wash the column with at least 20–30 mL DPBS.
Cover the top-filter with DPBS before closing the upper cap and the luer slip cap.
Measure each fraction for membrane vesicle concentration using an Izon qNano.
Determine the protein concentration of fractions by using a Pierce BCA protein assay kit.
Concentrate collected MV fractions to a final volume of 200 μL using Amicon Ultra-2 centrifugal filter devices with a cutoff of 3 kDa.
Equilibrate three Amicon Ultra-2 centrifugal filter devices.
Place the Amicon Ultra-2 filtrate devices into the filtrate collection tubes.
Load each device with 500 μL ice-cold, sterile filtered DPBS and cover with concentrate collection tubes.
Centrifuge at 4,000 ×g and 4°C for 60 min.
Discard the flow-through in the collection tubes.
Seal the filter devices again in the collection tubes.
Pool MV fractions 6–9 from each individual sample in a 1.5 mL low protein binding collection tube.
Invert the pool tube 3 times.
Load each filtrate device with 1.5 mL MV-containing sample and cover with concentrate collection tubes.
Centrifuge at 4,000 ×g and 4°C for 40 min.
Remove the filter devices from the centrifuge.
Disconnect the filter devices from the filtrate collection tubes.
Invert the filter devices tied to the concentrate collection tubes.
Insert the inverted filter devices in the centrifuge rotor.
Centrifuge at 1,000 ×g and 4°C for 2 min.
Remove the concentrate collection tubes from the devices.
Collect the concentrated serum and colon MV-containing samples with a volume of 200 μL in sterile low protein binding collection tubes.
Store collected samples at 4°C or long-term at -20°C.
Supplement the MV concentrate with 2 mM MgCl2 and 0.1 mM CaCl2.
Incubate sample with 25 U/mL benzonase for 30 min at 37°C.
Add 1 mM EDTA to inhibit benzonase activity.
Heat sample at 95°C for 5 min to stop the reaction.
